## Self-hosting cost vs a managed Llama API

Endpoints are portable; the bill is not. A self-hosted server is billed by the hour whether or not requests arrive, while a managed API is billed per token. The table compares the two on the factors that usually decide the choice.

| Cost factor | Self-hosted llama.cpp | Managed Llama API on Novita AI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What you pay for | GPU hours, rented or owned, plus engineering time | Input and output tokens |
| Billing while idle | You keep paying the hourly rate | Nothing |
| Price anchor | Novita GPU Cloud lists H100 SXM at $1.70 per GPU-hour and B200 SXM at $4.77 per GPU-hour | Llama 3.3 70B Instruct at $0.135 per million input tokens and $0.40 per million output tokens |
| Capacity and scaling | Fixed to the GPUs you run; you add more to grow | Elastic; the provider adds capacity |
| Model updates, quantization, tuning | Yours to run and re-verify | Provider-side |
| Data path | Requests stay on your hardware | Requests leave your network |
| Context window | Whatever the GGUF model and `-c` allow | As listed on the model page, for example 12,288 tokens for Llama 3.3 70B Instruct |

Token prices from the Novita AI model page and model list API, checked October 16, 2026; GPU rates from the Novita AI GPU Cloud page, checked October 16, 2026.

The gap is easiest to see on a worked example. Take a small application that processes 50 million input tokens and 10 million output tokens a month on Llama 3.3 70B Instruct. On the managed endpoint that is 50 × $0.135 + 10 × $0.40 = $6.75 + $4.00, or $10.75 a month. Run the same model yourself on one GPU that stays up, at the published H100 SXM rate of $1.70 per GPU-hour, and the month costs 730 hours × $1.70 ≈ $1,241, with or without traffic. The managed bill is about 1% of the always-on GPU bill, so self-hosting only closes that gap when you push roughly two orders of magnitude more traffic through the server — and only if one GPU can serve it.

That arithmetic is why the decision is really a utilization question, not a feature question. Self-hosting wins when the GPU runs hot enough that the flat hourly cost beats the per-token cost, which usually means a steady production workload rather than a bursty or early-stage one. Current GPU rates live on the Novita AI GPU Cloud page, and the model side is on the model catalog.

...

Use a managed Llama API when traffic is bursty or unproven, when you want to skip capacity planning, or when you need a large context window without buying the VRAM that holds it. Novita AI serves Llama 3.1 8B Instruct at $0.02 per million input tokens and $0.05 per million output tokens, and Llama 4 Scout with a 131,072-token context, so the managed side scales from a cheap small model to a very long context without a hardware decision. The same catalog also carries Llama 3.3 70B Instruct as the mid-size default.

results.title: Llama API Guide: Access and Pricing for Llama 3.3, 4 Scout, and 4 Maverick - Novita
results.author: Novita AI
highlights:
By Novita AI· October 16, 2026· 5 minutes of reading

...

There is no single “Llama API” to sign up for. Meta releases Llama as open weights, and Meta’s own developer platform no longer lists Llama models in its API catalog, so in practice you reach Llama through a third-party host — Novita AI, DeepInfra, or Groq today. Which version you pick (Llama 3.3 70B, Llama 4 Scout, or Llama 4 Maverick) sets your usable context window anywhere from 12K to more than 1 million tokens, and which host you pick decides whether you get a published per-token rate at all. The table below puts every host-and-version combination that is actually callable side by side.

## Hosted Llama API options at a glance

| Provider | Llama version | Input ($/1M tokens) | Output ($/1M tokens) | Context window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Novita AI | Llama 3.3 70B | $0.135 | $0.40 | 12K |
| Novita AI | Llama 4 Scout | $0.18 | $0.59 | 128K |
| Novita AI | Llama 4 Maverick | $0.27 | $0.85 | 1M |
| DeepInfra | Llama 3.3 70B | $0.10 | $0.32 | 128K |
| DeepInfra | Llama 4 Scout | $0.10 | $0.30 | 320K |
| Groq | Llama 3.3 70B | Contact sales | Contact sales | 131K |
| Groq | Llama 4 Scout / Llama 4 Maverick | Contact sales | Contact sales | Not published |
| Together AI | No Llama model in the current serverless catalog | — | — | — |
| Meta (first-party API) | Not offered | — | — | — |

Pricing and context windows come from each provider’s own current model or pricing catalog, checked October 16, 2026. Groq documents its Llama models on an enterprise tier priced by contract, with no published per-token rate; its API model list also includes Llama 4 Scout and Llama 4 Maverick. Together AI’s serverless catalog lists no Llama model, and Meta’s first-party developer platform does not list Llama at all.

Three patterns stand out. Novita AI is the only host in this set that serves all three versions with published per-token pricing. Llama 4 Maverick is the least widely hosted version — the hosts that publish a rate for Scout do not all add Maverick. And only two hosts here publish a per-token rate at all, Novita AI and DeepInfra, while Groq prices its Llama models by contract, so a like-for-like sticker comparison is not always available.

...

Novita AI is the only host here that carries all three versions with public pricing, and it exposes them through one OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `https://api.novita.ai/openai`. Llama 3.3 70B runs at $0.135 input / $0.40 output per million tokens, Llama 4 Scout at $0.18 / $0.59, and Llama 4 Maverick at $0.27 / $0.85. The window is the one number to check per version: Novita serves Llama 3.3 70B with a 12K window, so match it to your prompt length, while Llama 4 Scout and Llama 4 Maverick come with much larger windows on the same endpoint.

...

Forgetting that pricing moves. Per-token rates and served context windows on every host here change independently of this comparison. Re-check the provider’s own page before you size a production budget.

# Best Qwen API Pricing in 2026: Official vs Novita, OpenRouter, DeepInfra

By Novita AI· October 12, 2026· 5 minutes of reading

...

Qwen3.8-Max costs $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens on Alibaba Cloud’s own International pricing, and the exact same model costs $1.65 and $4.951 on DeepInfra. Alibaba Cloud publishes two official rate cards for this model depending on which deployment scope an account is activated under, and on the check date every other platform’s listed Qwen3.8-Max price matched one of those two cards rather than a third number. This guide compares five places to call Qwen’s flagship and flash models, shows which official rate each platform’s price lines up with, and gives a framework for choosing beyond the sticker price.

...

- Alibaba Cloud runs two official rate cards for the same Qwen models: an International tier (Singapore-activated accounts) at $2/$6 per million tokens for Qwen3.8-Max, and a Global tier (Beijing, Hong Kong, Frankfurt, US-Virginia, Tokyo) at $1.65/$4.951 for the same model.
- Novita AI, Together AI, and OpenRouter all price Qwen3.8-Max at $2 input / $6 output, matching Alibaba’s International tier exactly.
- DeepInfra prices the same model at $1.65 input / $4.951 output, matching Alibaba’s Global tier exactly.
- The same split holds for Qwen3.8 Flash: $0.15/$0.47 on the International tier (Novita AI, OpenRouter) versus $0.113/$0.382 on the Global tier (DeepInfra).
- Cache-read pricing lines up with the same two tiers: roughly one-eighth of the input price, at whichever tier price the platform lists.

### 2. Novita AI: International-tier pricing with broader platform fit

Novita AI prices Qwen3.8-Max at $2 per million input tokens, $0.25 per million cache-read tokens, and $6 per million output tokens, matching Alibaba’s International tier exactly.
